items.prompt:
When an environment changes, the plants and animals there can
A) be affected
B) never be affected
C) only get bigger
D) turn into rocks

steps: Environmental changes can affect living things.

items.prompt:
A drought dries up a pond. A good solution is to
A) add clean water
B) remove all the water
C) do nothing
D) add sand

steps: Adding water helps the animals meet their need.

items.prompt:
A solution has merit if it
A) helps the plants and animals meet their needs
B) costs the most
C) looks nice only
D) does nothing
items.answer: A) helps the plants and animals meet their needs

steps: Merit comes from solving the problem for living things.

items.prompt:
A road blocks animals from crossing. A solution with merit is
A) an animal bridge over the road
B) a taller road
C) more cars
D) nothing
items.answer: A) an animal bridge over the road

steps: A safe crossing lets animals move again.

items.prompt:
Why might animals move away when their environment changes?
A) They can no longer meet their needs there
B) They get bored
C) They always move
D) The weather is nice
items.answer: A) They can no longer meet their needs there

steps: Unmet needs cause animals to leave or struggle.

items.prompt:
A forest is cut down and birds lose nesting trees. A solution is to
A) plant new trees
B) cut more trees
C) pave the ground
D) do nothing

steps: New trees restore nesting places over time.

items.prompt:
A stream is blocked so fish cannot swim upstream. Which has MORE merit?
A) Removing the block
B) Doing nothing
C) Adding more blocks
D) Draining the stream

steps: Removing the block lets fish move upstream again.

items.prompt:
Planting new trees to help birds may take time because
A) birds do not like trees
B) the trees must grow before birds can nest in them
C) trees never grow
D) it does not help at all
items.answer: B) the trees must grow before birds can nest in them

steps: New trees need time to grow large enough for nesting.
